axisSelection.placement: Whichever axis you'll be tuning, please place it in an initial location so that it'll have space to move to the right (for X), backwards (for Y), and downwards (for Z).
axisSelection.connectFirst: Please connect to a device before starting the movement tuning wizard.

completion.accurate: Your {{axis}}-axis looks accurate, so you should be good to go!

distanceTravelled.instructions: Lastly, measure the distance travelled between the original mark and the current gantry location. Take your time when entering this value, a more accurate measurement will give you better tuning results.

markFirstLocation.instructions: First, mark next to the gantry in the location shown with your marker, pencil, or using a strip of tape.

moveAxis.instructions: Now move any distance you wish. A larger value will better tune your movement, just make sure you don't hit your machine limits. Once you are ready, clicked the Move Axis Button.

intro.accurateWork: If you're looking to use your CNC for more accurate work and notice a specific axis is always off by a small amount - say 102mm instead of 100 - then use this tool.
intro.variations: Since CNC firmware needs to understand its hardware to make exact movements, small manufacturing variations in the motors, lead screws, pulleys, or incorrect firmware will create inaccuracies over longer distances.
intro.testing: By testing for this difference using a marker or tape and a measuring tape, this tool will better tune the firmware to your machine.

landing.prepare: To know how much adjustment is needed, follow the steps below. Prepare:
landing.tape: 3 squares of tape marked with an 'X'
landing.ruler: A long ruler or measuring tape
landing.pointer: Put something pointed in the spindle like an old v-bit, tapered bit, pencil, or a pointed dowel
landing.position: Use the jog buttons to position your CNC near its front, left corner with the pointed tip almost touching the wasteboard, then continue below.
landing.skewedCuts: If your CNC is making skewed cuts (pictured), it's because the X and Y axes aren't squared to each other. This can be fixed.
landing.connectFirst: Please connect to a device before starting the squaring wizard.
landing.skewedCutsCaption: If the X and Y axes aren't squared to each other on your CNC then it will cause your cuts to end up skewed.

minor.title: Your machine is slightly out of square
minor.deviation: The deviation is minor ({{diff}}{{units}}) but you may want to adjust the right Y-axis rail to achieve better squareness.
minor.adjust: You can move your either the right y-axis rail forward by {{diff}}{{units}} or the left y-axis rail backward by {{diff}}{{units}}.

invalid.title: These measurements aren't possible
invalid.body: The diagonal (1-3) must be shorter than the bottom and right edges added together, and longer than the difference between them. Please check your measurements for a typo and restart the wizard to measure again.

eeprom.title: Other Recommendations
eeprom.intro: We also noticed from the results that your motor movement settings could be updated to improve your machines accuracy.
eeprom.dialogBody: This will update the X-axis ($100) and Y-axis ($101) step/mm values in your CNC firmware to the new ones below:
eeprom.warningBody: Updating Firmware values can affect your machine's accuracy. Make sure to verify the new settings after applying them.

markPoint1.label: Mark Point 1
markPoint1.description: First, we'll mark three points on your machine in a triangle. Stick the first tape to the wasteboard at the CNCs current position. The pointed tip should almost be touching the center of the X.

moveXAxis.label: Move X-axis
moveXAxis.description: Input the farthest your CNC can move in the X-axis to create a horizontal line.

markPoint2.label: Mark Point 2
markPoint2.description: Now mark the second location with the second piece of tape.

moveYAxis.label: Move Y-axis
moveYAxis.description: Input the farthest your CNC can move in the Y-axis to create a vertical line.

markPoint3.label: Mark Point 3
markPoint3.description: Place the last piece of tape with an X mark at the current position.

measure12.label: Measure Distance 1-2
measure12.description: Now, measure the distances between the points you've marked and enter them below. Measure the distance between points 1 and 2.

measure23.label: Measure Distance 2-3
measure23.description: Measure the distance between points 2 and 3.

measure13.label: Measure Distance 1-3
measure13.description: Measure the distance between points 1 and 3.
